paragraphs: The Citan 111 CDI has been part of the Citan range since 2012, and across the W415 generation uses the K9K — a 1.5-litre four-cylinder diesel sourced from Renault and shared with the Kangoo of the same era. It's a reliable workhorse engine in its own right, but injector failure and EGR clogging are well-documented patterns on the K9K, especially in vans that have spent a lot of time on short urban runs. The Citan 111 CDI was discontinued from the range, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every CITAN 111 CDI on the road.

cards.body: A 1.5-litre four-cylinder diesel fitted to the Citan 111 CDI from 2012 to 2021 across the W415 generation. Known for injector failure and EGR clogging over time — see the callout above. We replace injector seals, the EGR valve and timing chain components as standard on every K9K rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the Citan 111 CDI uses a Renault-sourced K9K engine across the W415 generation, parts compatibility and engine matching are straightforward when confirmed correctly. We always confirm your exact engine code via registration or VIN, generation (W415), and any ancillary or ECU considerations specific to your build. This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic Citan quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual van.
